svg.text: Configured, unconfigured, unreachable — three states, not two

Without the unconfigured path, all 569 backend tests would need a live database, and infra/cloudbuild.yaml's test step — a bare python:3.12-slim container with no Postgres — would fail on the first import.
unit tests, CI, a laptop with no Postgres
No database is opened, and none is needed.
The rows the last good import run wrote.
Does not fall back to fixtures.
This column is the only one that refuses.
A laptop with no Postgres still runs.
Persisted in Cloud SQL, not in the process.
Does not fall back to memory.
The write is surfaced, never dropped.
The refusal rule applies to state 3 only
• A database that is configured and unreachable is the only
case that refuses. States 1 and 2 both serve figures.
• In state 3 book_source refuses and Store refuses. Neither
degrades to fixtures, and neither degrades to memory.
The unconfigured path is not a convenience
• Without it, all 569 backend tests would need a live database.
• infra/cloudbuild.yaml's test step is a bare python:3.12-slim
container with no Postgres — it would fail on the first import.
• So state 1 is what keeps the test contract and CI intact.
debt-migrate exits non-zero; the new revision never takes traffic.
This is exactly why cloudbuild.yaml sequences migrate before deploy-api.
Odoo unreachable, or refuses the login
The run is recorded FAILED. Serving degrades ODOO → last good landing rows → SHEET.
The transaction rolls back; the previous run keeps serving.
It does NOT fall back to fixtures or to memory.
The write is refused and surfaced to the officer.
The slot is empty and a figure
"RUNNING and REFUSING are both honest, and LEAKING is not."
A configured database that has gone away must never degrade to fixtures or to memory, because that failure would look exactly like success.
